A Five-Star Hủ Tiếu Experience
Jun 2026 • Solo
I ordered the Phnom Penh-style rice noodles (Hủ Tiếu Nam Vang), and it was outstanding. The broth was rich, savory, and satisfying. I highly recommend giving the bowl a thorough mix before eating so that the ingredients and flavors are distributed evenly. One thing I really loved was how the minced pork clung to the noodles, so you get the combination of noodles and meat in every bite. The noodles were cooked perfectly, with just the right texture, and all of the toppings were fresh and tender. This is easily one of the best dishes I've had in Ho Chi Minh City, and I'd gladly return to this restaurant just to order it again. It's definitely a must-try if you're visiting. I also ordered their signature Bánh Bao (steamed pork bun), which was delicious as well. I didn't expect it to be so huge. It's filling, flavorful, and another dish I'd definitely recommend.

You can tell this place is well-run, well-renovated, perhaps with second-gen contribution?
Dec 2024 • Friends
One of the most famous Hu Tieu joints over the past decades, and quite glad that with the new menu, we don't have to just hear from guides what's the origin story of this dish - they actually shared on their first page how the Hu Tieu story started when Vietnamese-Chinese (specifically, ChaoZhao or Teochew) from Cambodia/Khmer returned to Vietnam and made this dish famous in Vietnam. Quite thoughtful to include the origin story - since that's what many other Michelin places do too.

As for being well-run/ well-decorated:
- Well-run because even their raw vegetable-plates seemed to be individually prepared and packaged (i.e. not exposed to the elements).
- You could tell the servers were trained - always ready and attentive, but not obtrusive.
- Entire place was well-renovated with air-con, nice decor (even the giant fish tank). Loved that they are family-orientated and displayed huge family portraits as part of the slow-mo videos of their food preparations, taking pride in both. The hanging ladles and transparent bowls as chandeliers were a really nice touch.

As for the food itself:
- One of the few Hu Tieu places that still has braised blood curds in this dish. Prawns were adequately large and juicy. Sauces in both soup and dry were tasty.
- Other than the Hu Tieu, their herbal duck noodles was good too with its nourishing soup... and falling-off-the-bones kinda tender duck confit, with springy egg noodles.
- Friends were also impressed that their big pau didn't just have one, but two types of eggs - quail's and salted (duck's).
